# New GPU rates from October 5, 2026

From October 5, 2026 at 00:00 IST, new rates apply to NVIDIA H200, H100 and RTX PRO 6000 GPUs. They cover on-demand usage and any reserved plan started on or after that date. Current rates apply until then.

| GPU | On-demand rate until October 4 | On-demand rate from October 5 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA H200 SXM | $3.99/hr | $4.59/hr |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM | $2.69/hr | $3.49/hr |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | $1.89/hr | $2.19/hr |

Rates are per GPU-hour, in USD, excluding tax, and apply in all regions. From October 5, the pricing page will list the new on-demand rates, including INR. For new reserved plan rates, contact us at engineering@jarvislabs.ai.

## Why rates are changing

A global shortage of GPU memory (HBM3e and HBM3 on the H200 and H100, GDDR7 on the RTX PRO 6000) has raised the cost of this capacity. The new rates reflect that cost.

## What isn't changing

- Committed nodes stay at their existing price for the full contract period.
- Storage rates are unchanged.

Please contact engineering@jarvislabs.ai if you need help understanding the effect on your account.

results.title: Nvidia GPU Prices Surge 41% in Europe [2026]
results.author: Dr. Elena Marchetti
highlights:
European GPU buyers just got hard numbers confirming what their wallets already knew: graphics cards cost dramatically more than they did over the summer. A European GPU-market tracker following 179 Nvidia cards across 27 European retailers measured the average Nvidia graphics card price climbing from roughly €783 on June 28 to about €1,107 by September 28, a jump of 41.3% in three months. AMD’s Radeon lineup, tracked as a basket of 71 cards, rose more slowly but still painfully, from around €644 to €826, a 28.3% increase over the same window. The pricing data was reported on September 29, 2026 and corroborated independently by PCGuide, which attributed the surge to the ongoing memory shortage rather than any change in chip design or manufacturing cost for the GPUs themselves.

...

## Market impact beyond gaming PCs

The ripple effects reach well past gamers. Cloud GPU rental pricing has already moved in response to the same memory constraints, as covered in our report on Nebius raising AI cloud prices 21% while memory costs jumped 41%, showing that enterprise buyers of GPU compute face the identical upstream pressure as consumer shoppers, just denominated in cloud-hour pricing rather than retail sticker prices. Sesame Disk reported in October 2026 that Nebius raised GPU rates by 17–21%, with the H100 reaching $4.50/hour, and Jarvislabs increased H100 SXM pricing by 30% in the same month. Component resellers, system integrators, and prebuilt PC makers are all absorbing the same cost increases, and several have already begun passing them through in list prices for pre-assembled gaming desktops.

Retailers across Europe have reportedly started adjusting restock pricing more frequently than in previous years, a shift away from the relatively stable MSRP-anchored pricing that characterized most of the 2022-2024 period after the prior mining-driven shortage eased. That dynamic pricing behavior, where shelf prices change week to week rather than quarter to quarter, is itself a symptom of how volatile upstream memory costs have become.

System integrators building prebuilt gaming desktops face a harder problem than individual component buyers: they typically quote prices weeks ahead of actual assembly and shipping, which means a memory-driven price swing mid-quarter can turn a profitable order into a loss if the integrator doesn’t hedge with shorter quote windows or price-adjustment clauses. Several smaller system builders have reportedly shortened the validity window on their published prebuilt configurations as a direct response to this volatility, a practical, if unglamorous, sign of how deep the pricing instability has cut into normal retail operations.

results.title: Was trying out Jarvislabs.ai after quite some time today. | Sudalai Rajkumar - SRK
results.author: Sudalai Rajkumar - SRK
highlights:
Was trying out Jarvislabs.ai after quite some time today.

Apart from the GPU VMs that they used to provide, there were two new additions:
- Deployment Endpoints
- Hosted Models

Deployment Endpoints were a breeze to use for deploying custom HF models using vLLM / SGLang / Ollama and serving them for our applications. I was initially worried about the hourly billing for dedicated endpoints, but the scale-to-zero option helps scale the workers down to 0 during inactivity, thereby reducing costs.

Hosted Models are billed on a per-token basis and are relatively cheaper in rupee terms compared to other alternatives. Looking forward to seeing more models here.

results.title: Rental Rates for Older AI Chips Jump 25% as Demand Surges - Seoul Economic Daily
results.author: Seo Ji-hye, Kim Ji-young
highlights: Vessl AI raised its hourly rate for Nvidia H100 graphics processing units by 24.7% starting this month, following a string of price increases by U.S. neocloud providers such as CoreWeave and Nebius amid a surge in demand for artificial intelligence computing. Supply has tightened not only for the newest chips but also for older models as demand for high-performance GPUs jumps. Other Korean cloud providers also expect to raise GPU rates depending on supply conditions, raising concerns that higher costs of securing GPUs will weigh on service development at Korean AI companies and on government AI transformation, or AX, projects.

results.title: H100 Rental Prices Jump 22% in a Month as GPU Shortage Hits Firms and Labs - Seoul Economic Daily
results.author: An Hye-ji, Intern Reporter
highlights: - Key summary: Vessl AI, a domestic neocloud company, raised the hourly rate for Nvidia H100 chips on its VESSL Cloud service to $2.98 from $2.39 on the 1st of this month, a 24.7% increase. The price adjustment marks the start of similar moves in Korea after U.S. neocloud firms including CoreWeave and Nebius successively raised GPU rental rates. Vessl AI procures most of its roughly 7,000 GPUs through leasing. According to Ornn, an AI computing trading platform, the hourly cloud rental rate for the H100 rose 21.9% over the past month to $3.28 from $2.69, reaching about 70% of the price of the higher-end H200. The impact is spreading to industry and research, with some companies abandoning bids for government-led AI transformation projects because they could not secure GPUs, while universities and research institutes scale back the size of their research.

results.title: Everyone in the AI build is selling the same option to a different buyer
results.author: Haircut
highlights:
On 17 September, Nebius told customers that selected pay-as-you-go GPU rates rise 17% to 21% on 1 October. H100 goes from $3.85 to $4.50 an hour, H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50 and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50. By the 19th, the executed market went the other way. H100 was $2.85 versus $3.02 the day before and H200 was $5.13 versus $5.60. The new H100 card is 57.9% above the latest executed price.

I do not think that makes the list price useless though. Nebius still publishes preemptible rates of $2.15 for H100 and $2.45 for H200, and says a large multi-month reservation can get up to 35% off. Same accelerator, three prices. The fully flexible one is the one getting more expensive. You pay more if you want to turn up whenever you like.
